A.reason: Needs dozens of warm-up runs and about 390 contests per arm to detect a modest effect, and it only tunes edit-operator choice, which is a weak lever on final top-3 quality against a single agent.

B.reason: Loss-conditioned revision with a two-order different-family gate exploits information a lone agent lacks, and the no-reasons control arm isolates the mechanism, though the effect may be small and acceptance rates low.

C.reason: Cheap change to the finals judge that aligns selection with the benchmark's card format, rubric, and order-swap handling, and it can be replayed on existing finals logs, though it risks overfitting to LLM-rater taste.

D.reason: Raters see only cards, so removing critique residue and adding concreteness is a plausible and cheap win, and it can be tested by re-rating edited versus original cards offline, but it yields nothing if the gap is idea quality.

E.reason: Scoring-only portfolio selection is easy to replay offline, but it helps only on best-of-3 and would lose on mean rating, and finalists are often already diverse.

F.reason: Concentrating critique and mutation on boundary ideas is principled, but it needs 3-5 days and 30-50% extra cost, and in-loop judge overfitting can cancel the gain, so the effect is hard to isolate at 10 briefs.

G.reason: The repair loop with a template library depends on a check ledger that does not exist yet, costs 1-2 weeks and about 2x development tokens, and does not obviously improve rater-perceived idea quality.

H.reason: Executable-check critique is grounded, but many idea briefs are qualitative so most claims will be not_checkable, and it needs a sandbox, a new phase and extra tokens for uncertain gain.

I.reason: Putting the baseline inside the candidate pool with a displacement gate makes the output a selection from a superset of the baseline's ideas, so the system is unlikely to fall below the baseline, and displacement rate gives a direct measured outcome.

J.reason: Judge-reliability weighting is sound and can be replayed offline at zero token cost, but it needs about 300 externally rated votes and stable judge reliability, and gains are likely small.

K.reason: A learned residual selection head needs about 15 or more labelled briefs and risks Goodhart from panel-derived labels, and with few labels it collapses to the existing ranking.
